comments.body: 2026-10-27 re-triage: tooling feedback a_2neJkhNSM adds three 2026-10-24 instances in a kan round. A helper told "nothing else is queued for slot 2, so stay idle" ended its turn as asked; about 16 seconds later its maker got "went idle without posting." These are turns started by a message needing no answer, rather than idle compactions or declared waits. Keep this case separate from a_2nUsIZXNY, fixed by a29fb3e4, and from the repeat-notice fix b84df279. Forwarded the feedback here.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body:
2026-11-02, tool=muster, low severity: a Codex builder posted its completed commit and checks to its director, then went idle awaiting review. After two minutes @muster woke only the builder to say the director had not read the handoff because its prompt held unsent text. The builder read that notice and ended its turn without posting because there was no new work or question. About 18 seconds later @muster told the director that the builder "went idle without posting to you since it went to work" and might have ended on an error.

This is another no-reply turn, but the input is Muster's own held-wake notice rather than a stay-idle instruction from the director. A notification-only turn should not create a fresh unreported-work warning. No workaround was applied; an extra standing-by post would add another wake without advancing the review.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-02, Foreman integrator cactus with helpers sequoia, guppy and quill: four more in 20 minutes. Twice the same case as this card: guppy and quill were told to hold until another worker's stage landed, did so, and each raised 'went idle without posting'. Twice a new variant: sequoia ended its turn waiting on its own two reviewer helpers (marble, blossom, one still working), which is waiting on work, not idle without reporting. Suggest skipping the notice while the helper has helpers of its own that are working, or have posted to it since it last reported.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-06, Foreman: a reviewer helper answered another agent (not its maker) with muster msg post, twice in 4 minutes, and its maker got 'went idle without posting to you' both times. Counting a post to anyone at the end of the turn would cover this.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Another instance from tooling feedback a_2neJkhNSM, 2026-11-09 in agent-engine: wind's last turn only dismissed a Heads up notice in anvil's pane, after wind had already posted its review (#9). Muster then told anvil 'wind went idle without posting to you since it went to work 2 minutes ago', which read as a failed review until anvil checked the pane. (Muster no longer holds on that notice since 1013c711, so this particular trigger will stop.)
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-09 instance, Lectern round: worker panda (slot 3) ended turns to wait on its own two reviewer helpers (stone, condor) after posting them briefs, and once while a background test ran under a declared wait. Muster twice told integrator lizard 'panda went idle without posting to you', though panda was mid-assignment and posted its done report minutes later. A worker waiting on its own helpers is not idle-without-posting.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body:
From the tooling feedback hub (a_2lt9THKQ6), five more instances:
- 2026-11-06 (devenv, an integrator): four helpers (two Claude Code, two Codex) were each told 'landed, stand by' or 'findings assigned, stand by', read it and went idle within 30s, and each time @muster woke the integrator with 'went idle without posting to you ... may have ended on an error': four wasted integrator turns in one afternoon.
- Muster 0.24.0: a Codex reviewer helper told its findings were accepted and to keep its context until fix commits arrive acknowledged in its pane and went idle as asked; Muster then posted the same notice to its maker, which cost a pane read to rule out an error.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-10-21, before 0.18.0, in a directed council with the helper on another machine. The maker was done with a helper's assignment and told it to stay idle until its next message. The helper read that and ended its turn without posting, as `extras/skill/council/SKILL.md` says to: "Pass the turn by ending it." About 21 s later the maker was told the helper "went idle without posting to you since it went to work", with the hint that its turn may have ended on an error.

The turn that read the stay-idle message counted as going to work, so its end raised `Need::Unreported` (`crates/muster-daemon/src/messages/makers.rs`). a_2luQuOfD1 (done, in 0.18.0) stopped compactions and declared waits from raising it, and MIP-7 section 4 lists those as not going to work. A message from the maker that asks for no reply is a case neither covers, and the only way a helper can avoid the notice today is the "standing by" post the council skill forbids.

Possibly: let `msg post` mark a message as needing no reply, and start no stretch of work for a turn whose only input was such a message. A simpler rule, exempting any short turn that only read a message from the maker, would also hide a helper whose turn failed while reading it.
title: A helper told to stay idle is reported to its maker as idle without posting
